cards.text: Right before this, the LORD called out people who dig deep to hide their plans from Him (Isaiah 29:15). Now Isaiah the prophet brings another message, and it opens like this: “Woe to the rebellious children,” declares the LORD. Those children have a plan, and it's not His.

cards.question: The rebellious children are carrying out a plan that isn't the LORD's. What do they form, against His will?
The LORD calls this plan one small slip, nothing more.

cards.text: The plan? Go down to Egypt and take refuge under the protection of Pharaoh, Egypt's king. Pharaoh's shade, friend. That's the whole sales pitch.

cards.question: Before they set out for Egypt, the rebellious children ask the LORD for His advice.
The LORD warns them that Pharaoh's protection will become their ___.

cards.text: Their princes are already at Zoan, and their envoys have made it all the way to Hanes. Meanwhile the farthest I ever traveled in my junk drawer was three inches, every time somebody yanked it open looking for tape.

cards.question: All that travel, and the LORD calls the Egyptians a people ___ to them.

cards.text: Next comes a burden against the beasts of the Negev, a land of hardship and distress, with lions, vipers and FLYING serpents. Friend, I jump when my oven timer goes off.

cards.question: Through that land of lions and serpents, how are they carrying their wealth and treasures?

cards.text: All that treasure, hauled to a people of no profit to them. Egypt's help is futile and empty, and so Egypt gets a new name.

cards.question: Egypt's help is futile and empty. What is Egypt called?

cards.text: Then comes an order: go write it on a tablet in front of them, and inscribe it on a scroll. Not a sticky note on the fridge, friend. A SCROLL.

cards.question: Why does this message about Egypt need to go on a tablet and a scroll?

answers.text: To be a witness for the days to come
To be carried ahead to Pharaoh
To be signed by the princes

cards.text: Here's how these people are described: rebellious, deceitful, unwilling to obey the LORD's instruction. Then they hand the seers an order of their own: “Stop seeing visions!”

cards.question: They tell the prophets not to prophesy the truth to them. What do they want to hear instead?

cards.text: They don't want a prophet, friend. They want a FORTUNE COOKIE, and they've still got something to say about the Holy One of Israel.

cards.question: The people ask the prophets to bring them closer to the Holy One of Israel.

cards.text: Now the Holy One of Israel answers. They rejected this message, and they're trusting in oppression and relying on deceit.
He says their iniquity is like a breach about to fail, a bulge in a high wall. You know that crack in the wall at home you keep saying you'll deal with someday? Yeah. That one.

cards.question: Their iniquity is like a bulge in a high wall about to fail. How will the collapse come?

cards.text: And when it goes, it breaks in pieces like a potter's jar. Shattered.

cards.question: When the potter's jar shatters, a few pieces will still be big enough to scoop coals from a hearth.

cards.text: Not one usable shard, friend, and I've dropped a cookie box before, so I KNOW you can usually find a corner. Then the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, tells them how they would have been saved.

cards.question: What does the Lord GOD say they would have been saved by?
The people were willing to take the way of quiet confidence the Lord GOD offered.

cards.text: Instead, they say no, they'll flee on horses, swift horses. Repentance and rest, offered FREE, and they said, nah, we'll take the horses.

cards.question: They plan to ride swift horses, but their pursuers will be ___.

cards.text: And friend, the running only gets worse. Picture me the day a fly got into the bakery.

cards.question: How many of their enemies will it take to make a thousand of them flee?
After all that fleeing, they will be left ___, like a pole on a mountaintop.

findings.problem: The rebellious children are the people the whole message is about, but the card never says simply who they are. The baker isn't told these are the LORD's own people. Verse 9 calls them 'children unwilling to obey the LORD's instruction,' and Isaiah 1:1 sets Isaiah's visions over Judah and Jerusalem, which can be cited.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The Holy One of Israel first appears here (Isaiah 30:11), but the card never says simply that this is a name for God. Card 18 and all of stop 2 depend on the baker knowing who this is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This is a which-name question, but both wrong answers are made up. 'Rahab Who Runs Ahead' and 'Rahab the Strong Tower' aren't real details from anywhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: Verse 8 only says 'write it on a tablet' and never says what 'it' is. The question calls it 'this message about Egypt,' which decides something the text leaves open. Card 13 correctly says only 'write it.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The cookie box joke doesn't click. Dropping a box doesn't shatter it, and it isn't clear what 'a corner' you can usually find refers to. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Card 6 says the Lord GOD tells them 'how they would have been saved,' and card 7 asks what they 'would have been saved by.' That wording already tells the baker they didn't take that way, which rules out True before card 8 asks whether they were willing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The setup joke ('the day a fly got into the bakery') is about running from one tiny threat. That points straight to 'Just one' on card 12 and rules out 'Ten thousand' and 'A whole army.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
